description: We're StarMonitor, a two person team focused on bringing realistic solutions to the self monitoring problem among astronauts, especially on long missions. From delays in communication and treatment to an inability to get data on astronauts' bodies in real time, StarMonitor aims bring health data to our astronauts' fingertips.
summary: StarMonitor is a health monitoring app intended to help astronauts monitor their own care in space, especially on missions longer than 30 days. It can give basic information on possible next steps if a reading is irregular, such as temperature, heart rate, or other readings, as well as record information from blood, urine, and saliva tests. It then makes a chart of each factor, so the information is visualized. Without StarMonitor, astronauts could be fumbling through thick binders of medical information looking for a treatment plan. With Starmonitor, it's all in the portal.
details:
StarMonitor is a health monitoring app that uses user input data to track astronauts' health in space. It has the potential to connect to both the 1Drop blood testing system and the holter monitor that astronauts wear in space, as well as ECG and wearable temperature tracking technology to put users' health information at their fingertips. This data is then put on a point to point graph, able to show trends and whether their data falls in a healthy range. If it isn't within a healthy range, the health recommendations page will give intervention advice from its database. With this all at their fingertips, astronauts will be able to catch any problems that arise and treat them faster than ever before, leading to better healthcare in space.

StarMonitor also has a gamified aspect, where every day that users input their health data, a small cat named Mars gets a little bit closer to Earth. When the mission is done and the astronauts go home, so will Mars the cat. This incentivizes regular login and brings a happy aspect to the usually sterile quarters astronauts are accustomed to in space, which likely will positively affect crew mental health.

StarMonitor is intended to let astronauts operate independent of the Flight Surgeon when it comes to their healthcare, especially in Mars missions where delays can reach up to 50 minutes.

StarMonitor is coded in JavaScript and HTML, Mars the cat was drawn digitally on IbisPaint, and the StarMonitor logo was designed in Canva with a base from Feather Icons. We considered the health risks in space, both physical and mental, and the communication gaps between ground control and a Mars project.
